title: Any request without X-Forwarded-For receives 'direct-local' mutation authority — full anonymous control if port 3000 is reachable outside the gateway
description: The gate treats absence (or whitespace) of X-Forwarded-For as proof of a loopback local process and allows the request (operator.ts:87-89). Only Caddy stamps XFF; the Next servers themselves (package.json:6 'next dev -p 3000', :8 'bun .next/standalone/server.js') are not configured in source to bind loopback-only, and next.config.ts sets no bind option. If :3000 (or the standalone port) is reachable from any external network, every mutating route is anonymous-open with 'direct-local' authority — the entire operator-key law is bypassed. A direct connection that self-supplies a private XFF also passes (first hop decides, :88).
claimed_root_cause: Trust decision keyed on a header's absence rather than on the socket's actual locality; binding/firewall configuration is not present in the repository to enforce the loopback assumption.

verdict.allowed -> request proceeds to any POST handler
representative sink: POST executes queued tasks via executeTaskOnce; all other mutating routes equally reachable

title: Anonymous GET /api/health boots the organ-guardian loop and spawns organ processes — a state-changing GET the central gate classifies as public
description: GET /api/health (src/app/api/health/route.ts:94-107) unconditionally calls ensureOrganGuardian() (:97) — which boots a setInterval(60s) guardian loop (organ-guardian.ts:108-114) — and reviveOrgans() (:104), which probes all organs and spawn()s '/usr/local/bin/bun run dev' for any DOWN organ (health/route.ts:63-85, spawn at :81, 90s per-organ backoff), logging revival events to guardian.log (:42). Because isMutatingRequest returns false for plain GETs without ?force (operator.ts:74-82), the central proxy (the only authority control in the app) passes this route to the public internet through Caddy's default handle (Caddyfile:15-22): an anonymous external caller can force-respawn organs against the operator's process-state decisions (throttled only by the 90s backoff), read revival details including PIDs from the response, and drive guardian.log writes.
root_cause: Method-based mutation classification in src/proxy.ts (GET=public) does not match the actual side effects of GET /api/health; the revival logic was embedded in the health read path without adding a force/key condition.
intended_behavior: Public GETs are read-only; process spawning and background-loop booting are owner actions requiring direct-local/loopback origin or x-operator-key (or an explicit ?force, which would key-gate them).

title: Mutating API endpoints accept cross-site requests using only the private-network source IP as the ambient credential — no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site binding anywhere
description: resolveOperator grants full mutation authority ('private-net') to any request whose XFF first hop is a private-range IP (operator.ts:87-90). Caddy stamps X-Forwarded-For from remote_host (Caddyfile:18, replace not append), so a browser inside the private network acquires owner-level mutation authority on every /api route with no cookie, no token, and no Origin/Referer/Sec-Fetch-Site validation anywhere in src (grep: zero matches). Any website such a browser visits can silently fire state-changing POSTs: the strongest sinks need no body at all — /api/sovereign/chain-repair?confirm=repair-fork-1045 rewrites ledger tail hashes and the export file (chain-repair.ts:41,143-147,74-77) via a plain HTML form POST; /api/sovereign/ops/tick auto-approves and executes pending handoffs (ops/tick/route.ts:55,183,196); /api/tasks parses req.json() regardless of content-type (tasks/route.ts:15) creating QUEUED tasks that worker/tick later executes (LLM spend).
root_cause: Network position (source IP) is treated as an authentication credential for mutations; browsers present that credential ambiently to cross-site requests, and the central proxy performs no origin check to distinguish first-party from cross-site use of it.
intended_behavior: Per the gate's own doctrine (operator.ts:1-3), mutations should require a local process (loopback) or the owner key; a browser-issued cross-site request should be rejected via an Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site allowlist in proxy() or by requiring x-operator-key even for private-net callers.

title: fabric-heartbeat pull-and-restart pipeline executes origin/main code with zero in-repo integrity verification, under a PAT-backed push identity
description: Every 15 minutes (and 20s after boot, GIT_PULSE_FIRST_MS) gitPulse runs 'git pull --rebase origin main' (index.ts:657) with no commit pinning, no author/committer or signature check, and no path allowlist on fetched content. The pipeline then deliberately makes fetched code execute: the Task-119 law touches any organ's index.ts whose state files the rebase replaced (:692-709), forcing bun --watch to load the fetched modules inside organ processes; appGuard respawns 'bun run dev' from the same tree (:771); the only in-repo gate ('node .zscripts/leak-scan.mjs --staged', :635) is itself origin-sourced across pulses (it runs pre-pull on a tree shaped by prior pulls, so a landed commit can disable the secret gate at a later cycle) and scans secret patterns only — never code provenance. The heartbeat auto-commits and pushes any working-tree change ('git add -A' → commit → push origin main) under the GitHub PAT from upload/pat.env (name only) via the credential helper (.zscripts/git-credential-pat.sh), and on non-superset heals replaces the live db/custom.db with origin/main's blob (:528-538). Organs and the app run with the Steem WIF env names, OPERATOR_KEY, and vault files on disk — so executed fetched code reaches every secret the machine holds.
claimed_root_cause: No integrity handoff exists between origin/main and execution: the privileged automation treats origin as trusted-by-definition without commit pinning, author allowlist, signature verification, or a path allowlist, and its one gate (leak-scan) guards secret patterns — not code provenance — while being fetched code itself.

title: Caddy :81 forwards any caller to any loopback port via ?XTransformPort= with no authentication or allowlist
description: The root Caddyfile (:2-13) matches every request carrying query XTransformPort and reverse-proxies it to localhost:{query.XTransformPort} (:7), preserving method, path, remaining query and the attacker-supplied Host header (XFF overwritten to real client). There is no basic_auth/forward_auth/IP restriction and no port allowlist, so every organ port (dex 3010, witness 3050, keeper 3051, metrics 3060, grid 3070, arb 3071, council 3072, vault 3080, app 3000, and any other loopback listener) is reachable by unauthenticated external callers of :81 — the port the repo's own threat model calls the single public door (docs/SURVIVAL.md:112). Behind it sit zero-auth mutating endpoints (grid POST /halt /resume /cycle, arb POST /halt /resume, council POST /cycle /deliberate, vault-guardian POST /census /heal /drill, chain-witness GET /witness + /bench), and arb/metrics/heartbeat/keeper/witness additionally bind 0.0.0.0 — a second, gateway-independent external path. The dex repo's deploy/Caddyfile.public documents the intended hardened posture ('no public XTransformPort'; passthrough confined to 127.0.0.1:8081 with a {3010,3003} allowlist).
claimed_root_cause: Query-parameter-controlled upstream selection exposed on the public listener; the organs' loopback binds — the only isolation — are intentionally traversed by this rule, and the known hardening pattern (allowlist + loopback-only operator site) was applied in the dex repo but not to the root Caddyfile.

title: saos-arb /resume unconditionally lifts the manual kill-switch and both halt/resume run with zero authority checks
description: saos-arb (:3071) exposes POST /halt (:608-613) and POST /resume (:614-620) with no credential, no shared token and no header inspection. /halt writes the halt file with reason 'manual' — the owner's emergency stop. /resume sets halted=false, resets the error counter and unlinkSync(HALT_PATH) UNCONDITIONALLY, so a single unauthenticated POST defeats a manual kill-switch that cycle() explicitly treats as an owner decision auto-revival must not override (:468-486, esp. 472-474) and that healthJson promises stays (:581). The organ binds 0.0.0.0 (Bun.serve without hostname, :589) and the Caddyfile passthrough reaches :3071 from outside. The platform's own organ-mutation control pattern (repos/saos-dex operator-auth fail-closed x-saos-operator) is simply absent here. The dex book the arb trades on is declared simulation (index.ts:14), which limits financial blast radius but the explicit control defeat is complete.
root_cause: Mutating handlers implemented without any authorization mechanism, and /resume does not distinguish manual halts from auto-halts, contradicting the organ's own Task-115 doctrine.
intended_behavior: Manual kill-switch may only be lifted by the owner (operator key or loopback-local process); /resume must refuse reason==='manual' halts exactly like the auto-revival path does.

title: POST /api/dex/desk-ledger accepts unauthenticated receipt inserts because its 'signature' is an unkeyed public hash
description: The only POST route on the dex without operatorAuth (38 of 57 sibling route files are gated). title: Shadow→live migration broadcasts sell orders while the external-value anchor is unavailable, bypassing the Task-117 absolute no-sell fail-closed
description: engine.cycle() enforces 'no anchor → absolutely no sells' by forcing skipSide='sell' when floor===null (engine.ts:466) and gating ladder sells (:676), counter sells (:593) and requotes (:804) on it. The shadow→live migration loop (§4.6, engine.ts:480-515) is the one sell path outside that gate: it cancels a shadow sell only when `floor !== null && o.price < floor` (:492); when the anchor is unavailable (floor===null) that condition is false and the shadow sell falls through to broadcastLimitOrder (:504) at its recorded price — no anchor check, no skipSide guard (the buy side got the skipSide guard at :498, the sell side did not). Keys auto-restore via vault-guardian censusCycle auto-heal (vault-guardian/index.ts:73-78 → recover.ts:302-319, landSteemEnv :256), flipping engine mode to live (engine.ts:117-119), and the anchor-collapse scenario was measured live (Task-117: binance IP-reset + coingecko 429 → sells below parity 0.1029 < 0.1101).
root_cause: Migration sell guard is cancel-only-if-below-floor (`floor !== null && o.price < floor`) instead of failing closed when floor is null; the skipSide==='sell' guard applied to buys (engine.ts:498) was never applied to sells in this loop.
intended_behavior: Task-117 doctrine (engine.ts:415-425, 464-466, 802-804): with no external-value anchor, no sell may ever go live — the migration loop must cancel-or-hold shadow sell rows when floor===null, exactly as it already does for below-floor rows when the floor exists.

title: Identity-line anchor accepts any single-source positive value with no cross-check or plausibility bounds — hostile/corrupted feed steers the live sell floor
description: getExternalMarks() takes the first responding source (sticky first-wins, market.ts:302-313), validates only `p > 0` after parseFloat of the raw JSON field (parsers at :276/:283/:291 — NaN/negative rejected, but no Number.isFinite anywhere in the feed path so parseFloat('1e999')=Infinity passes, no upper bound, no plausibility clamp), then identityLine=steemUsd/sbdUsd and floor=identity×(1+50bps) (engine.ts:417-418) directly price live sell orders (engine.ts:682-685, broadcast :863-869) and drive the below-floor purge (re-anchoring orders onto the new floor). The 0.4% deadband (:270, applied :337-340) only suppresses small moves; one lying/compromised source can move the anchor (and rewrite state/marks.json, :341/:345) arbitrarily in a single refresh and stays first in the probe order while it responds. No median-of-sources, no deviation-vs-previous-mark bound beyond the deadband, no absolute plausibility band. Infinity produces an absurd floor (trading freeze); finite wrong values are the loss-bearing case (below-parity sells — exactly the measured Task-117 incident).
root_cause: Single-source trust with minimal validation (>0) and sticky first-wins ordering; the sell-floor policy is defined by an unvalidated feed value with no robust aggregation or sanity band.
intended_behavior: Anchor values must be finite, absolutely plausible, and bounded per step: reject non-finite and values outside an absolute plausibility band; reject single-refresh moves beyond a bound vs the previous anchor (freeze last-good anchor instead); on disagreement → hold last-good or fail closed (no sells).

execution.attacker_perspective: A compromised or lying feed source returns steemUsd far below market once; identityLine and the sell floor collapse; the ladder prices live sell orders at the hostile floor and the below-floor purge re-anchors existing orders onto it — operator STEEM sold below external value; no authentication or cross-check rejects the value, and the sticky ordering keeps the poisoned source first while it responds.
payloads: feed response bodies such as {"price":"0.000001"} (binance), {"steem":{"usd":0.000001}} (coingecko), {"quotes":{"USD":{"price":0.000001}}} (coinpaprika) — any positive number is accepted; parseFloat('1e999')=Infinity also passes
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: the value passes the only validation (p>0), becomes marksCache/marks.json, becomes floor, and prices live sell orders.

remediation.strategy: Surgical hardening now: Number.isFinite check in every parser, absolute plausibility band on identity inputs, and a single-refresh step bound (freeze last-good anchor on oversized moves). Full median+MAD aggregation across all sources as the follow-up (the dex price-proof module already implements that discipline for the same data class).

title: vault-guardian key-custody operations (/census, /heal, /drill) are triggerable by any caller with zero authority checks
description: vault-guardian (:3080, bind 127.0.0.1, index.ts:104) exposes POST /census, POST /heal and POST /drill (:125-140) with no authority check. /heal forces heal() — the vault restoration pipeline that re-derives key material and lands upload/steem.env ONLY when the census failed (recover.ts:306-319; on an intact vault it is a key-file no-op, :321, but still re-runs the in-memory recovery drill); /census runs censusCycle which auto-invokes heal() when !steemOk||!allClear (index.ts:73-78); /drill runs the recovery drill. All three publishReceipt-append to upload/vault-guardian-log.jsonl (:22, :53-54) with no rotation. Responses expose booleans/fingerprints only (no secret disclosure), but the custody state machine itself is invocable anonymously via the gateway passthrough.
root_cause: Sensitive custody actions on a loopback-trust organ with no authority check; gateway passthrough makes the loopback assumption false.
intended_behavior: Custody state transitions require the operator token (fail-closed), matching the platform's organ-mutation pattern.

title: Complete Steem key-recovery envelope (ciphertext + passphrase + seal wallet) co-located in one repository — repo read access equals Steem active-key access
description: vault-guardian/recover.ts reconstructs the headcorner Steem active/posting/memo WIF51 private keys fully automatically from GitHub repo roshpinacare-sys/Saosmartwallet: the archive passphrase is read from recovery-meta-2026-09-12.json stored in the same repo (:159), used to decrypt KEYS-ACCESS-2026-09-12.tar.enc (openssl aes-256-cbc-pbkdf2, 300k, :162); the decrypted vault.json WIFs open GateConfig.keySeals (wallet DB — local-first at upload/vault-rescue/wallet.db with the same repo's git history as fallback, :100-113) via scrypt(N=32768)→AES-256-GCM (:127-142); the recovered master decrypts VaultEntry rows into WIFs, chain-verified (:191-218), then lands upload/steem.env 0600 (:238-259, chmod :257). The cipher, its passphrase, and the seal metadata all live in the same repository/host, so the only boundary protecting the Steem active key and wallet master key is that repo's read ACL (plus the read-only PAT at upload/pat.env, name only). The zero-human design law is stated at index.ts:8.
claimed_root_cause: Split-knowledge is absent: the encrypted key archive's passphrase is co-located with the ciphertext and with the keySeal wallet DB in the same repository, nullifying the archive's AES-256-CBC-PBKDF2 envelope for any principal with repo read access; the intended control is solely the repo's privacy/ACL.
